title: Why India Dropped Yashasvi Jaiswal Despite Back-to-Back ODI Centuries for the England Tour
excerpt: Yashasvi Jaiswal was dropped despite scoring two centuries in his last three ODIs.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Yashasvi Jaiswal was dropped despite scoring two centuries in his last three ODIs.
  • Selectors prioritized experience, bringing back Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and Jasprit Bumrah.
  • Critics demand clarity on veterans' roles ahead of the 2027 World Cup.
  • The ODI series in England is crucial for India's World Cup preparations.

  • Yashasvi Jaiswal has been dropped from India's ODI squad for the three-match series against England despite scoring centuries in two of his last three ODI innings, including an unbeaten 110 against Afghanistan.
  • The selectors brought back Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli (subject to fitness), and Jasprit Bumrah, prioritizing experience over form ahead of the 2027 World Cup.
  • Former India batter Sanjay Manjrekar has criticized the decision, calling for transparency on whether veterans have a defined roadmap for the 2027 World Cup.
  • The three-match ODI series in England (July 14-19) is part of India's build-up to the 2027 World Cup in South Africa.

Yashasvi Jaiswal has scored hundreds in two of his last three ODI innings. He just hit an unbeaten 110 off 86 balls against Afghanistan. By any conventional measure of cricketing form, the 24-year-old left-hander earned his place on the flight to England.

The selectors disagreed. When the BCCI announced India's 15-member squad for the three-match ODI series against England, Jaiswal's name was conspicuously absent — replaced by the returning Virat Kohli, whose inclusion remains subject to fitness clearance after a hamstring injury sustained during the IPL 2026 final.

![Rohit Sharma — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1e/Prime_Minister_Of_Bharat_Shri_Narendra_Damodardas_Modi_with_Shri_Rohit_Gurunath_Sharma_%28Cropped%29.jpg)

Experience Over Form

The decision reflects a clear philosophical choice by India's selection committee: for the marquee assignments that lead to the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, experience trumps recent performance. Rohit Sharma retains his place to open alongside captain Shubman Gill. Kohli slots back into the top order. Jasprit Bumrah returns for his first ODI appearance since the 2023 World Cup final.

> **""Yashasvi has scored two hundreds in his last three ODIs."**

Jaiswal was drafted into the Afghanistan series specifically to cover for Kohli's injury. He seized that opportunity with a century in Chennai that showcased exactly what India have often sought at the top of the order — fearless intent combined with the ability to convert starts into substantial scores.

![Virat Kohli — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/9b/Virat_Kohli_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)

His record is stark: 116 not out against South Africa, then after a gap, 4 and 110 not out against Afghanistan. Two hundreds in three ODI appearances is a conversion rate that demands attention.

The Veterans vs. Next Generation Debate

Former India batter and commentator Sanjay Manjrekar has been particularly vocal about the omission. "Yashasvi has scored two hundreds in his last three ODIs. He made 116 not out against South Africa, then after a gap, scored four and a hundred," Manjrekar said. "Anyone opening in India's strong ODI side will get opportunities, and Yashasvi has made the most of them."

![Jasprit Bumrah — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/02/Jasprit_Bumrah_in_PMO_New_Delhi.jpg)

"Yashasvi has scored two hundreds in his last three ODIs. Anyone opening in India's strong ODI side will get opportunities, and Yashasvi has made the most of them."

— Sanjay Manjrekar, former India cricketer

Manjrekar urged the BCCI selection committee to provide clarity on whether Rohit Sharma and Kohli are being retained with a definitive roadmap for the 2027 World Cup. If the veterans have no clear timeline for stepping aside, he argues, developmental slots must go to the next generation.

The Full Squad

India's squad for the England ODIs: Shubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli (subject to fitness), Shreyas Iyer (vice-captain), KL Rahul (wicketkeeper), Ishan Kishan (wicketkeeper), Washington Sundar, Axar Patel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Harshit Rana, Arshdeep Singh, and Gurnoor Brar.

Other notable changes: Axar Patel returns in place of Harsh Dubey, while Harshit Rana is back after recovering from a knee injury that forced him to miss the T20 World Cup and IPL. There remains no place for Ravindra Jadeja, with Washington Sundar continuing as the spin-bowling all-rounder. Hardik Pandya also misses out, still recovering from back and leg injuries.

Looking Ahead

The three-match series — with matches at Edgbaston (July 14), Sophia Gardens in Cardiff (July 16), and Lord's (July 19) — serves as a continuation of India's build-up to the 2027 World Cup. The tension between backing proven match-winners and blooding the next generation will persist through the cycle. For Jaiswal, the question is not whether he deserves a place, but whether the establishment will create one before the World Cup itself forces the issue.
